texts.preamble: Raveendranath @ Chefmaster Mohanan vs Food Safety Officer on 27 November, 2024 W.P.(C) Nos.36684, 30827, 34172, 34613, 35660 of 2024 1 2024:Ker:89781 In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present The Honourable Mr.Justice Mohammed Nias C.P. Wednesday, The 27Th Day Of November 2024 / 6Th Agrahayana, 1946 Wp(C) No. 36684 Of 2024 Petitioner: Raveendranath @ Chefmaster Mohanan, Aged 64 Years S/O.Sudhakaran, Shef Master, Papanasam Beach Road, Varkala P.O., Thiruvananthapuram, Residing At Ambadi Nivas, Kappil P.O. Edava, Varkala Circle, Thiruvananthapuram District, Pin - 695141 By Advs. M.Balagovindan
texts.facts: The petitioner submits that he is a retail seller of Ice cream who took a room for rent in the year 2024 from the 4 th respondent. Petitioner submits that he had obtained a licence from the Commissioner of Food Safety under the provisions of the FSSAI Act, 2006. Petitioner conceded that despite receiving Ext.P5 notice from the Municipality on 06.08.2024, directing him to function only with a trade licence, he has not stopped the business or applied for a licence. 2. Upon admission of the writ petition, an interim order was granted by this Court on 03.09.2024 and the same is still in force. Taking note of the fact that the petitioner has not made any application for a licence as directed in Ext.P5, there will be a direction to the petitioner to file an appropriate application for a trade licence before the Municipality within a week from today. The petitioners were served with Ext.P4 notice directing him to take a licence. Admittedly, the petitioners are functioning without a trade licence from the Municipality. 2. Taking note of the fact that the petitioner has not made any application for a licence as directed in Ext.P4, there will be a direction to the petitioners to file an appropriate application for a trade licence before the Municipality within a week from today. The same person had filed Appeal No.136 of 2024 before the Tribunal. The Municipality seeks an expeditious disposal of both the above cases. Both appeals were preferred against orders passed under Section 406(3) of the Kerala Municipality Act, alleging unauthorised constructions. The Municipality submits that in view of the pendency of these appeals and the interim stay granted, they are unable to take any action against those constructions which were totally unauthorised. W.P.(C) No.34613 of 2024 is filed by the person who is alleged to be a tenant under the 4th respondent. The petitioner submits that he was granted a temporary licence for a temporary shed upto 31.03.2023 and thereafter, the Raveendranath @ Chefmaster Mohanan vs Food Safety Officer on 27 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126073255/ 9 Municipality was refusing to accept the application for renewal of licence submitted by the petitioner. 2. The Municipality had filed a counter, stating that proceedings were taken against the owner of the building alleging unauthorised constructions and they are pending before the Tribunal for Local Self Government Institutions. The same has been directed to be disposed of by orders in W.P.(C) No. 34172 of 2024. However, the facts remain that the petitioner in W.P.(C) No.34613 of 2024 is presently running without a trade licence. The petitioner was issued with Ext.P5 notice directing him to take a licence. Admittedly, the petitioner is functioning without a trade licence from the Municipality. EXHIBIT P12 TRUE PHOTO COPY OF E MONEY ORDER SLIP ISSUED TO THE PETITIONER FOR HAVING SENT RS. 1000/- TO THE RESPONDENT VARKALA MUNICIPALITY. EXHIBIT P13 TRUE COPY OF THE PHOTOGRAPHS SHOWING CONSTRUCTION OF COMMERCIAL BUILDING VERY NEAR TO THE SEA AND WITHIN CRZ-2.
